source: Rice, Mysore and Coorg vol II
what_is_said: headquarters of the Jagadguru, "proprietor of the surrounding tract"; supported by the magani revenues plus Rs. 1,000 a month from the Mysore State; disciples' gifts on tours spent on hospitality
quote: Besides the revenues of the magani, the religious establishment is supported by a grant of Rs. 1,000 a month from the Mysore State.

source: Rice, Mysore and Coorg vol II
what_is_said: The Sringeri magani forms an endowment of the math of the Smarta Brahmans … The country from its inaccessible character was virtually independent
quote: The Sringeri magani forms an endowment of the math of the Smarta Brahmans, founded in the 8th century by the Saiva apostle Sankaracharya

source: Rice, Mysore and Coorg vol II
what_is_said: a Smārta guru resides; the founder "invested by the Shringeri swami, about 500 years ago, with authority to administer to the Mahratta Brahmans of that sect"; burnt by the Maratha army 1791
quote: The first founder of the matha was invested by the Shringeri swami, about 500 years ago, with authority to administer to the Mahratta Brahmans of that sect.

what_is_said: jāgīr in Koppa taluq, population 9,144, "administered in imitation of the Mysore revenue system"; granted 1346 by Harihara I and brothers (inscription), re-established by Keladi Venkatappa Nayak 1621; revenue c. Rs. 50,000 a year plus Rs. 12,000 from the State
quote: A jagir in Koppa taluq, belonging to the chief matha of the Smarta Brahmans. It is administered in imitation of the Mysore revenue system

what_is_said: population 1,987, a municipality; 120 temples; maṭha with the Śāradā temple, Vidyāśaṅkara temple; Navarātri feeding of "all classes"; Rs. 50,000 magani revenue plus Rs. 1,000 a month; Liṅgāyats allowed to blow conches in its processions
quote: It is the head-quarters of the Jagad-guru, the high priest of the Smarta Brahmans, who is proprietor of the surrounding tract of country.

what_is_said: seat of a matha connected with the one at Sringeri, guru appointed by the Śṛṅgeri Svāmi c. 500 years ago "to minister to the Smartas of Mahratta descent"; the Marathas under Parashuram Bhau who burnt it in 1791 were threatened with excommunication, averted by gifts
quote: It is the seat of a matha connected with the one at Sringeri, the original Guru having been appointed by the Sringeri Swami about 500 years ago to minister to the Smartas of Mahratta descent.

what_is_said: maṭha of about two acres; 12th svāmī; devotees Brahmans, Rajputs, Marāṭhās, Shimpis, Panchals, Gabits; Rs. 30,000 a year from thirty inām villages (15 in Kolhapur, 5 Belgaum, 3 Nizam's, 2 each Patvardhan, Satara, Savantvadi, 1 Bijapur); svāmī tours levying contributions. Local account: Shankarbharati left Śṛṅgeri c. 1570, was refused re-entry, founded a maṭha at Kudalgi, then maṭhas at Kolhapur and Sankeshvar under Bijapur patronage
quote: Shankarbharati or Devgosavi a successor of Vishvarupacharya left Shringeri about 1570 on a pilgrimage to Benares … the head at Shringeri did not allow him to enter

institution: Śaṅkarācārya tomb, Śiva temple and monastery
what_is_said: Sachchidanand Shankaracharya "said to have come from Shringeri in Maisur" under the second Peshwa (1720–40), died at Nasik; successor Brahmanand died within a month; tombs and temple built by Savai Madhavrao (1774), rest-house by Nana Fadnis, monastery by Naro Shankar (1750); Rs. 500 from Pimpalner revenues and Rs. 288 Government grant
quote: In the time of the second Peshwa (1720-1740) Sachchidanand Shankaracharya is said to have come from Shringeri in Maisur and stayed in Nasik.

what_is_said: one of the city's two large maṭhs; the upper works of the Ambābāī temple "added by Shankaracharya" (Rs. 1 lakh); spire and domes of another temple added "by a Shankaracharya of Sankeshvar"
quote: Kolhapur has two large monasteries or maths, one belonging to the Sankeshvar Svami and the other to a Jain Svami.

what_is_said: an alienated village belonging to Sankeshvar Svami, population 1,036 (1881)
quote: Khidrapur, an alienated village belonging to Sankeshvar Svami

what_is_said: the head-quarters of the spiritual Teacher or guru of the Havig or Haig Brahmans; 45th head, a minor; line traced to a disciple admitted by Śaṅkarācārya at Benares, via Ujjain and Gokarn; built and endowed by the Sonda chief. No Śṛṅgeri maṭha is described anywhere in Kanara's Places
quote: The Honalli or Smart monastery is the head-quarters of the spiritual Teacher or guru of the Havig or Haig Brahmans.

what_is_said: built by Shankarji Keshav Phadke after the fall of the Portuguese (1739); Government grant Rs. 421, managed by a committee
quote: the great temple of Shankaracharya Svami, which was raised by Shankarji Keshav Phadke in honour of the restoration of the old faith, on the fall of the Portuguese in 1739

what_is_said: c. 1750 "the Brahmanical pontiff" met the Jain high priest in Poona and agreed, "it is said by bribing the Shankaracharya", to a Jain temple in a non-Brahman quarter
quote: About 1750 the Jati or high priest of the Jains and Shankaracharya the Brahmanical pontiff happened to meet in Poona.

what_is_said: income nearly Rs. 14,000; head appoints managers of three temples, one at Conjeeveram (see madras/README.md, finding 3)
quote: There is an important Smarta religious institution here in the math of Sankaracharya

institution: (no maṭha) act of the Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru
what_is_said: the Ananteshvara image from Nellikar "was installed at Karkal by Shree Jagadguru Narasimha Bharati Swamiji of Sringeri Matha"
quote: was installed at Karkal by Shree Jagadguru Narasimha Bharati Swamiji of Sringeri Matha

what_is_said: The image of Sharadamba in the second temple is just like that of Sharadamba at Sringeri.
quote: just like that of Sharadamba at Sringeri

what_is_said: formerly it was a part of the Sankesvar Math, the link was broken about 50 years ago (see revised/README.md)
quote: now the Kolhapur math is known as Karvir Pitha

what_is_said: 1883 text reprinted; adds the monastery "built in Panchavati by Nana Phadnavis" to which the Dravida Brahmans are attached, and Dr Kurtakoti ("Shankaracharya of Karaveer") at his Panchavati maṭh
quote: Sachchidanand Shankaracharya is said to have come from Shringeri in Mysore and stayed in Nasik
